title: JoyoFit watch navigation message (version 1)
description: One message between JoyoFit (phone, package com.joyodigitama.joyofit) and the JoyoFit Navi watch app (bundle com.joyodigitama.navi) over Wear Engine P2P: link service 0x34, command 0x01, P2P cmd 2 (data), payload = this object as UTF-8 JSON, at most 1000 bytes, one object per message, no trailing newline. The P2P layer acknowledges every data message with cmd 3 code 0xcf; nothing in the JSON is an acknowledgement. See protocol/README.md, 'P2P (f) Watch navigation'. Distances are whole metres, times whole seconds. Unknown fields must be ignored by the receiver; an unknown `t` must be ignored (logged), never answered.

v.description: Protocol version. A receiver drops a message whose `v` it does not know.

t.description: Message type. Phone -> watch: start, turn, prog, off, reroute, arrive, end, hb. Watch -> phone: hello, pause, resume, stop.

n.description: Sequence number of the sender, one counter per direction: 1 for the first message of a navigation session (phone) or of an app launch (watch), +1 per message, after 2147483647 back to 1. A receiver ignores a message whose `n` equals the previous one it took from that sender (a P2P retry).

street.description: Street or path name from OpenStreetMap via OSRM, cut to 48 characters by the phone; empty when the way has no name or the turn was derived from the route's shape.

dir.description: Maneuver. `depart` = the first instruction (head off along the route), `arrive` = the destination is the next point, `roundabout` comes with `exit`.

empty.description: A message with no fields besides the envelope.

start.description: Phone -> watch, first message of a session and the answer to `hello` and to `resume`. The watch shows the navigation screen.

dest.description: Name of the route (or the destination), cut to 48 characters.

totalM.description: Length of the route still to go when the message was sent.

etaS.description: Seconds to the destination: from the recent speed, before any speed from the route's activity default (walk 1.4 m/s, run 2.8 m/s, ride 5 m/s).

turn.description: Phone -> watch, the instruction the wearer acts on next. Sent when the instruction changes (a turn was passed, a reroute), on `hello`/`resume`, and when the distance crosses 200 m and 50 m (the watch vibrates once at <= 200 and at <= 50).

distM.description: Metres along the route from the wearer to the maneuver.

street.description: The street the maneuver leads onto.

exit.description: Roundabout exit to take; only with dir `roundabout`, and only when OSRM gave it.

next.description: The instruction after this one, only when it follows within 150 m (a quick double turn).

prog.description: Phone -> watch, progress: at most every 5 s, sooner when the distance to the turn changed by 10% or more since the last `prog`.

remM.description: Metres to the destination along the route.

end.description: Phone -> watch, the session is over; the phone stops sending. `arrived` after `arrive`, `stopped` when the user (phone or watch `stop`) ended it, `error` when the phone could not go on (location lost for good, route unusable).

hello.description: Watch -> phone when the watch app opens (a lite-wearable app does not run in the background, so the wearer often opens it mid-route). A navigating phone answers with `start`, the current `turn` and a `prog`, then `off` when the wearer is off the route; a phone that is not navigating does not answer (the P2P layer still acknowledges with 0xcf). `resume` is answered the same way.

x-joyofit.pauseResume: `pause` stops `turn`/`prog`/`off` from the phone (`hb` goes on every 30 s, the engine keeps tracking); `resume` makes the phone send `start`, the current `turn` and a `prog` again. `stop` ends the session: the phone answers `end {why:"stopped"}`.
x-joyofit.offRoute: `off` once when the wearer has been more than 40 m from the route for 10 s; then `reroute` when the phone asks OSRM for a new line (only with network), followed by a fresh `turn`. Back on the route without a reroute: a fresh `turn`.
